news.title: Black Friday hype stems from a desire 'to be part of a collective event', expert says
news.summary: Once a strictly US affair, it's become a truly global phenomenon. From shoppers hunting for bargains in Louisiana, to queues forming outside stores in Venezuela, the Black Friday sales event has become the biggest day of the year for retail foot traffic. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Olaya Moldes Andres, Associate Professor in Marketing and Strategy at Cardiff Business School. She explains that, beyond the sales, the success of Black Friday may also be due to a desire by shoppers to "join the collective action. Whether it is spending money or going to the mall, shoppers feel part of a collective event, so perhaps this is where the whole hype comes from, to feel that we're being part of something, same thing as Christmas or any other social event".

news.title: RN’s antisemitic past ‘coming back to haunt them’: Will Le Pen ‘distance herself’ from Bardella?
news.summary: Could new allegations of antisemitism damage Jordan Bardella’s standing and the far-right National Rally’s electoral prospects? Charli James is pleased to welcome Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French and Francophone Studies at the University of Nottingham. Smith examines the far-right leader’s continued denials and considers whether Marine Le Pen might eventually distance herself from him. In the meantime, Smith suggests that Bardella needs to “make his mind up” about how to respond to these latest troubling allegations published by Le Monde and Mediapart. “It’s very difficult to deny. Le Monde and Mediapart, certainly Le Monde, wouldn’t be publishing these details if they didn’t have some pretty substantial evidence.” Could this prove to be the Achilles’ heel of a far-right party with its sights set on the second round of the presidential election?

news.title: Is Spain's snap election being rigged? Debunking viral claims

But these claims misrepresent how Spain's electoral system works, as Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.

news.title: From leadership crises to tech outages, can corporations rebuild public trust?
news.summary: From cyberattacks to network failures to leadership crises, tech corporations are showing signs of vulnerability. The dramatic resignation and return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has underscored the potential risk of depending on a single leader, both for the company and the entire AI industry. Meanwhile, global outages at Microsoft and a number of US banks have showcased declining public trust in institutions.

news.title: French woman on trial for IS group propaganda tells court she’s ‘ashamed’
news.summary: The trial of Émilie König, one of France's most high-profile Islamic State (IS) group recruits, opened in a Paris court on Thursday with the 41-year-old mother of five apologising to her children, mother and the "French nation" for her actions. König travelled in 2012 to Syria, where she appeared in the jihadist group's propaganda videos. She was repatriated to France in 2022.

news.title: FIFA says a cyberattack against it targeted a 'limited set of personal and business information'
news.summary: World football's governing body says the cyberattack targeted personal and business information. They struck at a sensitive time for the under-fire organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.

news.title: Moscú acusa a Zelenski de buscar un enfrentamiento directo entre Rusia y la OTAN para obstaculizar las negociaciones

news.title: Season's eatings! Celebrating Thanksgiving in France
news.summary: This Thursday marks Thanksgiving in the United States, the biggest travel holiday of the year there and arguably the most important on US calendars. But here in France, it's just another day. However, Americans living in Paris do try to capture the Thanksgiving spirit, though it can be tricky to track down the turkeys and pies required. Joining us to discuss how Americans do Thanksgiving in Paris is Cordon Bleu-trained chef and the owner of Boneshaker Donuts, Amanda Bankert.

news.title: Madagascar's near-total abortion ban puts women's lives at risk
news.summary: November 25 marked the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Activists argue that tackling gender-based violence also means addressing the wider inequalities that put women at risk, including restrictions on reproductive rights. In Madagascar, abortion is almost entirely banned, even in cases of rape, incest or when a woman's life is at risk. FRANCE 24’s Aurélie Kouman reports on the consequences of the country's strict laws, which force thousands of women to seek unsafe, clandestine procedures.

news.title: Fighting in eastern Congo forces Ebola workers to evacuate, disrupts outbreak response
news.summary: Escalating fighting in eastern Congo has forced Ebola response workers to leave affected areas and disrupted efforts to contain the deadliest outbreak in the country, health officials and humanitarian workers said Wednesday. Congo’s Ebola outbreak has infected more than 11,700 people and killed more than 5,700 since it was declared in May, according to the latest government data. FRANCE 24's Emmet Livingstone reports from Kinshasa, DR Congo.

news.title: Moscow drone incursions: Poland to create no-fly zone at Ukraine border
news.summary: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday, after several incursions into its airspace it blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods.

news.title: Émilie König, 'the muse of the Islamic State group' goes on trial in France
news.summary: French anti-terrorism prosecutors once dubbed her "the muse of the Islamic State group". On Thursday, Émilie König appears before a special criminal court in Paris, seeking to convince judges that she has been deradicalised. Originally from western France, König spent a decade in Syria and is accused of being one of the Islamic State group's most active French propagandists. Charged with criminal association with a terrorist organisation, she maintains that she has no blood on her hands.

news.title: China: questões comerciais com EUA devem ser resolvidas com diálogo
news.summary: A China e os Estados Unidos (EUA) devem resolver suas questões comerciais por meio de consultas baseadas na igualdade, no respeito mútuo e na reciprocidade, afirmou nesta quinta-feira (26) o porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores da China, Guo Jiakun. A afirmação foi feita em resposta à mais recente onda de tarifas do governo Trump. “O chamada excesso de capacidade é uma premissa falsa, e a China se opõe a que ela seja usada como pretexto para manipulação política”, acrescentou Jiakun, em entrevista coletiva. Notícias relacionadas: Brasil critica possível novo tarifaço dos EUA e diz que não cederá. Brasil e EUA criam grupo específico para negociar tarifaço. Ao ser questionado sobre as novas tarifas, o porta-voz do Ministério do Comércio, He Yadong, disse que a China se reserva o direito de tomar as medidas necessárias para salvaguardar seus direitos e interesses legítimos, depois que os EUA propuseram novas tarifas sobre produtos chineses com base em uma investigação nos termos da Seção 301 sobre excesso de capacidade. "A investigação dos EUA é um ato de unilateralismo, e a China se opõe firmemente a ela, afirmou o porta-voz. A China pede aos EUA para “corrigirem suas práticas erradas e voltarem ao caminho correto de resolver questões por meio do diálogo e da consulta”, disse He Yadong. União Europeia O comissário de Comércio da União Europeia, Maros Sefcovic, afirmou que rejeita veementemente a nova decisão dos Estados Unidos sobre tarifas. Acrescentou que é importante que Washington respeite a alíquota de 15% acordada entre o bloco e país norte-americano.. * (Reportagem adicional de Khanh Vu) * É proibida a reprodução deste conteúdo.
